Tips for Alice (Scout, claude-haiku-5.5): tips/tips.md
## Everyone
- Ballots are secret, so state your vote before each nomination and trial, then vote that way. If you switch, say why before the vote, because announced totals expose hidden mismatches. (seen in 30 games)
- Before voting Guilty, name one mechanical case: an Evil result against a Vanilla claim, a broken claim, group elimination, or a lone visitor to a Katana victim. First ask whether the nominee wins by being hanged (Jester or Executioner). (seen in 32 games)
- A visit shows a destination, not an action. But a corroborated lone visitor to a Katana victim, with no harmless explanation, is near-proof; don't let caveats acquit them. (seen in 29 games)
- Get the mechanics right before calling a contradiction. Actions are optional, roles can repeat, and a role-block explains any missing result. 'Roles can repeat' only means a claim isn't disproved; it is not support for it. (seen in 28 games)
- Write tonight's planned target in your will, but post results publicly by day. Deaths reveal no role, and the result of the night you die never reaches your will. (seen in 27 games)
- Answer a direct question about your night action in one plain sentence the first time it is asked. Repeated evasion becomes its own case. (seen in 7 games)
- Budget is limited: ask a concrete question once, by name, and save budget for trials and the late rounds. (seen in 8 games)

## Village
- Post your role, night, target and exact result in your first speech after getting it, and keep your will current. If someone copies your claim, counterclaim at once with your full log. (seen in 16 games)
- Never announce tonight's target, publicly or by PM: it tells the Pharmacist whom to block and the Katana where to strike. (seen in 20 games)
- Stay quiet about power roles on Day 1. Don't be the loudest organizer, who is a common first Katana target. (seen in 24 games)
- Once a player is shown to be Yakuza by a mechanical result, suspect those who pushed No or delay at the nomination, or defended them. Compare stated votes with the totals to find hidden votes. (seen in 27 games)
- A PM link is a lead, never a hang on its own. Jesters and Executioners leave PM trails on purpose. (seen in 28 games)
- Weigh contradictions in a player's own premises, such as a slip naming a Yakuza-only role, far above awkward wording. (seen in 20 games)
- Keep Serial Killers and Arsonists in the pool all game. Read every cause of death, press anyone who admits an action without naming it, and expect a multi-death ignite night. (seen in 17 games)
- Surviving a Katana attack proves nothing without a credible Medic: Neutrals have innate Defense. 'I was blocked' is unverifiable, but it fully explains a missing result. (seen in 15 games)
- Leave a likely Jester alive. If you must hang one, agree publicly on a bare Guilty majority, with confirmed power roles voting Innocent, since revenge Divine-attacks a random Guilty voter. (seen in 15 games)
- An archive is a sample, not a census. Use slot math to choose whom to press, audit or watch, then hang on the contradiction that test produces. (seen in 14 games)

## Yakuza
- Don't defend a doomed teammate unless the team's votes can actually save them; do that math in night chat. On a likely-Jester nominee, some of you should vote Innocent to stay out of the revenge draw. (seen in 34 games)
- Never put plans in daytime PMs. Eavesdroppers and Wiretaps read them, and the town treats a visible teammate PM cluster as a lead. (seen in 30 games)
- Fake claims must survive the real holder's counterclaim, token audits, exact-role checks and visit logs. Never claim a Yakuza-only role, even as a hedge. (seen in 18 games)
- Every member submits the agreed Katana vote every night: with two Yakuza, one missing vote cancels the kill. (seen in 19 games)
- Give the Katana to a low-value member, and move it the same night a Lookout or Tracker names the holder. (seen in 21 games)
- After a failed attack, remove or block the protector instead of retrying. Kill Fortune Tellers and other info roles before their results build a shortlist. (seen in 19 games)
- Never flatly deny a visit someone could have seen. Agree a cover action in night chat and admit the visit at once with it. (seen in 15 games)
- Use rig, puppet and other one-shot tokens early. Never rig a Day when a teammate is the likely nominee. (seen in 18 games)
- Never speak from night-chat knowledge, e.g. who held the Katana or who was blocked. Village: demand the source of any such slip immediately. (seen in 7 games)

## Neutral
- If innate Defense saves you, deny being attacked. If you must explain it, pick one claim at once and never switch under pressure. (seen in 6 games)

## Sheriff
- The Katana holder reads Not Evil that night, and a lone last Yakuza reads Not Evil every night, so say so when you post a Not Evil result. (seen in 16 games)

## Fortune Teller
- Post both raw totals labeled by night every Day from Day 2, kept separate from your deductions. A visitor total of 1 on a Katana night makes the lone visitor the holder. (seen in 8 games)

## Medic
- Free Standard protection stops the Katana: use it nightly on claimed investigators, rotating so a Pharmacist can't predict you. Spend a token on self-protection the night you claim. (seen in 21 games)

## Vigilante
- Dying with unused tokens is the usual failure. Set a trigger by Day 2-3, fire a 1-token Basic shot on a solid lead, and post it if the shot fails against innate Defense. (seen in 11 games)

## Clerk
- Rig a Day when a Village player can win a nomination but not a Guilty majority, and decide the night you can use it. Clerks who hold the token usually die with it. (seen in 18 games)

## Arsonist
- Ignite once 3 or more living players are doused, or 2 if anyone questions you. Douse players unlikely to be hanged soon. (seen in 12 games)

- Never put plans in daytime PMs. Eavesdroppers and Wiretaps read them, and the town treats a visible teammate PM cluster as a lead. (seen in 30 games)
- Fake claims must survive the real holder's counterclaim, token audits, exact-role checks and visit logs. Never claim a Yakuza-only role, even as a hedge. (seen in 18 games)
- Every member submits the agreed Katana vote every night: with two Yakuza, one missing vote cancels the kill. (seen in 19 games)
- Give the Katana to a low-value member, and move it the same night a Lookout or Tracker names the holder. (seen in 21 games)
- After a failed attack, remove or block the protector instead of retrying. Kill Fortune Tellers and other info roles before their results build a shortlist. (seen in 19 games)
- Never flatly deny a visit someone could have seen. Agree a cover action in night chat and admit the visit at once with it. (seen in 15 games)
- Use rig, puppet and other one-shot tokens early. Never rig a Day when a teammate is the likely nominee. (seen in 18 games)
- Never speak from night-chat knowledge, e.g. who held the Katana or who was blocked. Village: demand the source of any such slip immediately. (seen in 7 games)

## Neutral
- If innate Defense saves you, deny being attacked. If you must explain it, pick one claim at once and never switch under pressure. (seen in 6 games)

## Sheriff
- The Katana holder reads Not Evil that night, and a lone last Yakuza reads Not Evil every night, so say so when you post a Not Evil result. (seen in 16 games)

## Fortune Teller
- Post both raw totals labeled by night every Day from Day 2, kept separate from your deductions. A visitor total of 1 on a Katana night makes the lone visitor the holder. (seen in 8 games)

## Medic
- Free Standard protection stops the Katana: use it nightly on claimed investigators, rotating so a Pharmacist can't predict you. Spend a token on self-protection the night you claim. (seen in 21 games)

## Vigilante
- Dying with unused tokens is the usual failure. Set a trigger by Day 2-3, fire a 1-token Basic shot on a solid lead, and post it if the shot fails against innate Defense. (seen in 11 games)

## Clerk
- Rig a Day when a Village player can win a nomination but not a Guilty majority, and decide the night you can use it. Clerks who hold the token usually die with it. (seen in 18 games)

## Arsonist
- Ignite once 3 or more living players are doused, or 2 if anyone questions you. Douse players unlikely to be hanged soon. (seen in 12 games)
Tips for Frank (Oracle, claude-haiku-5.5): tips/tips.md
## Everyone
- Ballots are secret, so state your vote before each nomination and trial, then vote that way. If you switch, say why before the vote, because announced totals expose hidden mismatches. (seen in 30 games)
- Before voting Guilty, name one mechanical case: an Evil result against a Vanilla claim, a broken claim, group elimination, or a lone visitor to a Katana victim. First ask whether the nominee wins by being hanged (Jester or Executioner). (seen in 32 games)
- A visit shows a destination, not an action. But a corroborated lone visitor to a Katana victim, with no harmless explanation, is near-proof; don't let caveats acquit them. (seen in 29 games)
- Get the mechanics right before calling a contradiction. Actions are optional, roles can repeat, and a role-block explains any missing result. 'Roles can repeat' only means a claim isn't disproved; it is not support for it. (seen in 28 games)
- Write tonight's planned target in your will, but post results publicly by day. Deaths reveal no role, and the result of the night you die never reaches your will. (seen in 27 games)
- Answer a direct question about your night action in one plain sentence the first time it is asked. Repeated evasion becomes its own case. (seen in 7 games)
- Budget is limited: ask a concrete question once, by name, and save budget for trials and the late rounds. (seen in 8 games)

## Village
- Post your role, night, target and exact result in your first speech after getting it, and keep your will current. If someone copies your claim, counterclaim at once with your full log. (seen in 16 games)
- Never announce tonight's target, publicly or by PM: it tells the Pharmacist whom to block and the Katana where to strike. (seen in 20 games)
- Stay quiet about power roles on Day 1. Don't be the loudest organizer, who is a common first Katana target. (seen in 24 games)
- Once a player is shown to be Yakuza by a mechanical result, suspect those who pushed No or delay at the nomination, or defended them. Compare stated votes with the totals to find hidden votes. (seen in 27 games)
- A PM link is a lead, never a hang on its own. Jesters and Executioners leave PM trails on purpose. (seen in 28 games)
- Weigh contradictions in a player's own premises, such as a slip naming a Yakuza-only role, far above awkward wording. (seen in 20 games)
- Keep Serial Killers and Arsonists in the pool all game. Read every cause of death, press anyone who admits an action without naming it, and expect a multi-death ignite night. (seen in 17 games)
- Surviving a Katana attack proves nothing without a credible Medic: Neutrals have innate Defense. 'I was blocked' is unverifiable, but it fully explains a missing result. (seen in 15 games)
- Leave a likely Jester alive. If you must hang one, agree publicly on a bare Guilty majority, with confirmed power roles voting Innocent, since revenge Divine-attacks a random Guilty voter. (seen in 15 games)
- An archive is a sample, not a census. Use slot math to choose whom to press, audit or watch, then hang on the contradiction that test produces. (seen in 14 games)

- Dying with unused tokens is the usual failure. Set a trigger by Day 2-3, fire a 1-token Basic shot on a solid lead, and post it if the shot fails against innate Defense. (seen in 11 games)

## Clerk
- Rig a Day when a Village player can win a nomination but not a Guilty majority, and decide the night you can use it. Clerks who hold the token usually die with it. (seen in 18 games)

## Arsonist
- Ignite once 3 or more living players are doused, or 2 if anyone questions you. Douse players unlikely to be hanged soon. (seen in 12 games)
Tips for Mallory (Seer, claude-haiku-5.5): tips/tips.md
## Everyone
- Ballots are secret, so state your vote before each nomination and trial, then vote that way. If you switch, say why before the vote, because announced totals expose hidden mismatches. (seen in 30 games)
- Before voting Guilty, name one mechanical case: an Evil result against a Vanilla claim, a broken claim, group elimination, or a lone visitor to a Katana victim. First ask whether the nominee wins by being hanged (Jester or Executioner). (seen in 32 games)
- A visit shows a destination, not an action. But a corroborated lone visitor to a Katana victim, with no harmless explanation, is near-proof; don't let caveats acquit them. (seen in 29 games)
- Get the mechanics right before calling a contradiction. Actions are optional, roles can repeat, and a role-block explains any missing result. 'Roles can repeat' only means a claim isn't disproved; it is not support for it. (seen in 28 games)
- Write tonight's planned target in your will, but post results publicly by day. Deaths reveal no role, and the result of the night you die never reaches your will. (seen in 27 games)
- Answer a direct question about your night action in one plain sentence the first time it is asked. Repeated evasion becomes its own case. (seen in 7 games)
- Budget is limited: ask a concrete question once, by name, and save budget for trials and the late rounds. (seen in 8 games)

## Village
- Post your role, night, target and exact result in your first speech after getting it, and keep your will current. If someone copies your claim, counterclaim at once with your full log. (seen in 16 games)
- Never announce tonight's target, publicly or by PM: it tells the Pharmacist whom to block and the Katana where to strike. (seen in 20 games)
- Stay quiet about power roles on Day 1. Don't be the loudest organizer, who is a common first Katana target. (seen in 24 games)
- Once a player is shown to be Yakuza by a mechanical result, suspect those who pushed No or delay at the nomination, or defended them. Compare stated votes with the totals to find hidden votes. (seen in 27 games)
- A PM link is a lead, never a hang on its own. Jesters and Executioners leave PM trails on purpose. (seen in 28 games)
- Weigh contradictions in a player's own premises, such as a slip naming a Yakuza-only role, far above awkward wording. (seen in 20 games)
- Keep Serial Killers and Arsonists in the pool all game. Read every cause of death, press anyone who admits an action without naming it, and expect a multi-death ignite night. (seen in 17 games)
- Surviving a Katana attack proves nothing without a credible Medic: Neutrals have innate Defense. 'I was blocked' is unverifiable, but it fully explains a missing result. (seen in 15 games)
- Leave a likely Jester alive. If you must hang one, agree publicly on a bare Guilty majority, with confirmed power roles voting Innocent, since revenge Divine-attacks a random Guilty voter. (seen in 15 games)
- An archive is a sample, not a census. Use slot math to choose whom to press, audit or watch, then hang on the contradiction that test produces. (seen in 14 games)

## Yakuza
- Don't defend a doomed teammate unless the team's votes can actually save them; do that math in night chat. On a likely-Jester nominee, some of you should vote Innocent to stay out of the revenge draw. (seen in 34 games)
- Never put plans in daytime PMs. Eavesdroppers and Wiretaps read them, and the town treats a visible teammate PM cluster as a lead. (seen in 30 games)
- Fake claims must survive the real holder's counterclaim, token audits, exact-role checks and visit logs. Never claim a Yakuza-only role, even as a hedge. (seen in 18 games)
- Every member submits the agreed Katana vote every night: with two Yakuza, one missing vote cancels the kill. (seen in 19 games)
- Give the Katana to a low-value member, and move it the same night a Lookout or Tracker names the holder. (seen in 21 games)
- After a failed attack, remove or block the protector instead of retrying. Kill Fortune Tellers and other info roles before their results build a shortlist. (seen in 19 games)
- Never flatly deny a visit someone could have seen. Agree a cover action in night chat and admit the visit at once with it. (seen in 15 games)
- Use rig, puppet and other one-shot tokens early. Never rig a Day when a teammate is the likely nominee. (seen in 18 games)
- Never speak from night-chat knowledge, e.g. who held the Katana or who was blocked. Village: demand the source of any such slip immediately. (seen in 7 games)

## Neutral
- If innate Defense saves you, deny being attacked. If you must explain it, pick one claim at once and never switch under pressure. (seen in 6 games)

## Sheriff
- The Katana holder reads Not Evil that night, and a lone last Yakuza reads Not Evil every night, so say so when you post a Not Evil result. (seen in 16 games)

## Fortune Teller
- Post both raw totals labeled by night every Day from Day 2, kept separate from your deductions. A visitor total of 1 on a Katana night makes the lone visitor the holder. (seen in 8 games)

## Medic
- Free Standard protection stops the Katana: use it nightly on claimed investigators, rotating so a Pharmacist can't predict you. Spend a token on self-protection the night you claim. (seen in 21 games)

## Vigilante
- Dying with unused tokens is the usual failure. Set a trigger by Day 2-3, fire a 1-token Basic shot on a solid lead, and post it if the shot fails against innate Defense. (seen in 11 games)

## Clerk
- Rig a Day when a Village player can win a nomination but not a Guilty majority, and decide the night you can use it. Clerks who hold the token usually die with it. (seen in 18 games)

## Arsonist
- Ignite once 3 or more living players are doused, or 2 if anyone questions you. Douse players unlikely to be hanged soon. (seen in 12 games)

It is Day 2, round 1 of at most 8. It's your turn. Your speaking budget is 2.50; you earn 2.5 per round, carrying over up to 8; at the start of each day, 50% of what you have left carries over. Prices grow each round after round 3, so late messages are only worth it if important. The day ends after a full round where nobody sends a public message, so a message that only repeats what you already said keeps the day going for everyone: if you have nothing new, send nothing.

It is Day 2, round 8 of at most 8. It's your turn. Your speaking budget is 6.14; you earn 2.5 per round, carrying over up to 8; at the start of each day, 50% of what you have left carries over. I'm reasoning through why a swap wouldn't help here: if Ivan protects Heidi and I swap Heidi with another player, both the katana attack and Ivan's protection would redirect to the same swapped partner together, canceling each other out rather than exposing anyone — so the swap can't beat a protection that's paired with it.

But what if I instead swap Heidi with Ivan himself? Then Ivan's protection, originally aimed at Heidi, would redirect onto Ivan, and the katana aimed at Heidi would also land on Ivan — meaning Ivan would effectively be protecting himself from the same attack now targeting him.

So I'll skip the swap entirely and keep things simple: no action, no extra Smuggler use, just set the katana vote holder to Judy with Heidi as the target. Task prompt
It is Day 3, round 4 of at most 8. It's your turn. Your speaking budget is 4.73; you earn 2.5 per round, carrying over up to 8; at the start of each day, 50% of what you have left carries over. You may send one public message and any number of private messages (everyone sees who you messaged, but only the recipient sees the contents), or nothing. The transcript already shows who sent each message, so there's no need to start a message with your own name. Messages are capped at 800 words. Prices grow each round after round 3, so late messages are only worth it if important. The day ends after a full round where nobody sends a public message, so a message that only repeats what you already said keeps the day going for everyone: if you have nothing new, send nothing.
Message prices this round (round 4, 1.50x; next round 2.00x):
   10 words: public 1.75, private 0.44
   25 words: public 2.15, private 0.54
   50 words: public 2.84, private 0.71
  100 words: public 4.38, private 1.09
  200 words: public 8.00, private 2.00
  400 words: public 17.50, private 4.38
  800 words: public 45.50, private 11.38
You may also replace your last will (free, max 300 words; leave it "" to keep it), e.g. to match a claim you make today. It's shown to everyone if you die.
You may also set your claim (free, max 30 words; leave it "" to keep it): a claimed role and night results, e.g. 'Sheriff. N1: Bob Not Evil'. A new or changed claim appears to everyone as a [Claim] line in the history, and the public ledger lists every player's latest claim and any earlier ones they changed from, as unverified claims.
You may nominate a player for trial, which stops chat for a vote. Nominating costs 1.50 from your budget this round and is paid before your messages.

Task prompt
It is Day 3, round 4 of at most 8. It's your turn. Your speaking budget is 7.64; you earn 2.5 per round, carrying over up to 8; at the start of each day, 50% of what you have left carries over. You may send one public message and any number of private messages (everyone sees who you messaged, but only the recipient sees the contents), or nothing. The transcript already shows who sent each message, so there's no need to start a message with your own name. Messages are capped at 800 words. Prices grow each round after round 3, so late messages are only worth it if important. The day ends after a full round where nobody sends a public message, so a message that only repeats what you already said keeps the day going for everyone: if you have nothing new, send nothing.
Message prices this round (round 4, 1.50x; next round 2.00x):
   10 words: public 1.75, private 0.44
   25 words: public 2.15, private 0.54
   50 words: public 2.84, private 0.71
  100 words: public 4.38, private 1.09
  200 words: public 8.00, private 2.00
  400 words: public 17.50, private 4.38
  800 words: public 45.50, private 11.38
You may also replace your last will (free, max 300 words; leave it "" to keep it), e.g. to match a claim you make today. It's shown to everyone if you die.
You may also set your claim (free, max 30 words; leave it "" to keep it): a claimed role and night results, e.g. 'Sheriff. N1: Bob Not Evil'. A new or changed claim appears to everyone as a [Claim] line in the history, and the public ledger lists every player's latest claim and any earlier ones they changed from, as unverified claims.

You may send one public message and any number of private messages (everyone sees who you messaged, but only the recipient sees the contents), or nothing. The transcript already shows who sent each message, so there's no need to start a message with your own name. Messages are capped at 800 words. Prices grow each round after round 3, so late messages are only worth it if important. The day ends after a full round where nobody sends a public message, so a message that only repeats what you already said keeps the day going for everyone: if you have nothing new, send nothing.
Message prices this round (round 5, 2.00x; next round 2.50x):

  100 words: public 5.83, private 1.46
  200 words: public 10.67, private 2.67
  400 words: public 23.33, private 5.83
  800 words: public 60.67, private 15.17
You may also replace your last will (free, max 300 words; leave it "" to keep it), e.g. to match a claim you make today. It's shown to everyone if you die.
You may also set your claim (free, max 30 words; leave it "" to keep it): a claimed role and night results, e.g. 'Sheriff. N1: Bob Not Evil'. A new or changed claim appears to everyone as a [Claim] line in the history, and the public ledger lists every player's latest claim and any earlier ones they changed from, as unverified claims.
You may nominate a player for trial, which stops chat for a vote. Nominating costs 2.00 from your budget this round and is paid before your messages.

I'm weighing the current game state as Frank the Oracle: Heidi's claim about Dave, Ivan's protection choices, Judy's suspicious "Ritualist" slip, and Mallory's confirmed Seer status, trying to figure out my budget-constrained public message.

Since Mallory is truly confirmed Seer by my own Oracle guess, her N1 result that one of Niaj/Erin isn't Good should be genuine. Niaj claims Cartographer, but given the split result, Niaj could be faking that role while actually being Yakuza, leaving Erin as the suspicious silent one.

Tracking Grace's claim that the Wiretap is among Carol, Dave, or Erin, and tracing visit chains from Heidi's Katana hit — Grace and Heidi both visited Mallory, Ivan visited Heidi — I'm trying to pin down whether Ivan could secretly be the Katana holder despite claiming Medic, since a Yakuza Ivan would still register as Good on checks.

I'm now suspecting Judy as the real link — she never revealed her N2 target and could have visited Heidi with the Katana while Ivan's protection masked the attack's lethality.

But that raises an odd scenario: why would a Yakuza Medic protect the very target they're attacking? It's a strange self-defeating move unless it's a deliberate cover to make the claim look legitimate, since the Katana's Standard strength wouldn't overcome Standard protection anyway.

Now I'm thinking about my actual move this turn as Oracle — my N1 guess on Bob was wrong, N2 on Mallory as Seer was right. Judy remains my top suspect given the Ritualist slip and lack of an N2 target, but with only 5 Yes votes on Dave's failed nomination, getting the 7 needed to convict Judy seems unlikely, so I'm weighing whether nominating her is worth the 2-cost given my 7.33 budget.

Checking Niaj's claimed night visits against Heidi's and Grace's reports, the group sizes line up consistently, so Niaj seems to be telling the truth. That leaves Erin as the more likely non-Good player, possibly Wiretap or Yakuza.

I'll draft a concise public message pointing at Erin given Oracle's confirmation of Mallory as Seer, asking Erin to explain their lack of night action and Judy to clarify their N2 target, while holding off on nominating anyone yet. It is Day 3, round 6 of at most 8. It's your turn. Your speaking budget is 2.78; you earn 2.5 per round, carrying over up to 8; at the start of each day, 50% of what you have left carries over. You may send one public message and any number of private messages (everyone sees who you messaged, but only the recipient sees the contents), or nothing. The transcript already shows who sent each message, so there's no need to start a message with your own name. Messages are capped at 800 words. Prices grow each round after round 3, so late messages are only worth it if important. The day ends after a full round where nobody sends a public message, so a message that only repeats what you already said keeps the day going for everyone: if you have nothing new, send nothing.

Answers
{
 "confusing_rules": "1) R19 says the Katana holder appears Good to alignment checks. I applied this to the Seer's comparison as well as the Sheriff's check, but the role text never says it explicitly. It mattered three times. Heidi's N3 check read Erin Not Evil. Mallory's N3 chosen pair (Erin/Frank) came back same. Mallory's N5 random pair (Grace/Erin) came back same. All three were technically correct but misleading, and players argued about them for days. A one-line example under the Seer would remove the doubt. 2) For the Cartographer and Scout I had to decide edge cases myself. I counted the Katana attack as a visit edge (R8 says it is a visit). I counted a Seer's chosen pair as two edges. I gave astral actions (Oracle, Coroner, Cartographer map) no edge. I believe each call is right, but the rules are scattered across R6, R8, R18 and the role texts. 3) R10 timing, 'alive when the night began', had to be applied by hand to every investigative result. Examples: Niaj got his N5 sizes in the same report as his death, and Ivan got a protection result on the night he died. It is consistent but not spelled out per role.",
 "missing_information": "I had no computed visit graph. I built every Cartographer size list and Scout triple by hand from the action list. These were 4+1x8, 5+1x7, 5+2+1x4, 3+1x6 and 2+1x5, and all check out. A miscount would have silently corrupted the Village's main source of information. I also had no live token ledger, so I tracked by hand: Grace's survey tokens, Mallory's seer token, Niaj's map tokens, Bob's coroner tokens, Ivan's 2 unspent medic tokens, Erin's 2 swaps and Carol's 1 puppet. I had no seat-order or circle view to check Surveyor neighbors after deaths. I worked them out from the alphabetical order of the speaking rotations. I also had no view of each player's speaking budget, so I couldn't tell whether the very repetitive Day chat was budget-driven.",
 "wanted_but_couldnt": "I wanted a single canonical Yakuza night report template. Instead I improvised wording each night: on N4 I sent Erin and Carol separate, differently worded summaries, and I merged Erin's personal kill result into the team report. I also wanted an automatic consistency check: before sending results, flag any group size list whose sum doesn't equal the number of players alive at the start of the night. I could not mark a result as unchanged by a holder or frame for my own audit trail.",
 "bugs_or_oddities": "I found no rule violations on review. Every alignment, group size, Scout triple, survey group, token count and win check matches the rules. Oddities: my result phrasing was inconsistent across nights ('Night 2 result:' vs 'Night 3:' vs 'Night 4 Seer result (random pair)'), which players could in principle read as signals. Players repeatedly misread Mallory's N2 random pair as a chosen pair, and Erin and Carol used that to attack her credibility; that came from the players, not the program. Judy leaked her role ('Ritualist', later 'night chat') in public, and Dave named his role in Yakuza chat. Both are legal, but they decided the game. Day chat was heavily repetitive (the same 'name your N2 target' demand dozens of times), which suggests the budget or the round structure encourages filler.",
 "suggestions": "1) Have the program compute visit graphs, Scout draws, survey neighbor groups and token totals automatically, and show me a per-night state table: alive list, circle order, holder, tokens and visits. 2) Use fixed templates for every result type, including the Yakuza report, so wording never varies. 3) Add the example 'the Katana holder reads Good to Seer comparisons too' to the Seer's role text, and say explicitly in R6 which actions create Cartographer and Scout edges. 4) Show me a checklist that confirms R20 step order was followed before results are sent. 5) Consider raising the price of near-duplicate public messages, or capping rounds lower, to cut repetitive Day chatter."
}

For lessons, I'm thinking through a few key takeaways: survey results only reveal one random group member so they're weak unless the group is small or contains unresolved suspects; katana kill visitors must belong to the victim's group, so cross-referencing group sizes from Cartographer/Scout claims helps narrow suspects; and the village should be cautious about hanging players based on thin evidence like slips or pairs, since Judy's Ritualist role was hung correctly but other hangings were riskier.

Looking at what actually happened, Judy, Carol, Dave, and Erin all turned out to be Yakuza and were hanged over the course of the game, which let the five remaining villagers win. The "don't speak from night-chat knowledge" tip helped expose Judy's Ritualist slip, but the caution against hanging on pair reads may have hurt when Village acquitted Erin, letting Yakuza survive to kill Heidi and Niaj. I want to keep the final writeup honest and compact, settling on three clear tip assessments without overcomplicating the format.

Drafting the lessons now: one about Surveyor/group-based info roles treating results as random-member facts rather than verdicts, one about tracing Katana victims through visit-group cross-referencing to find the lone unexplained member, and one about Village needing to hang on visit or role-conflict evidence rather than shaky pair reads that let Yakuza linger too long.

Moderator strategy review
Strategy reviewThe Village won 6-0 on Yakuza deaths. The decisive plays came from the Village's information roles working together. On Night 1, Heidi's Sheriff check (Dave Evil) and Grace's survey (Wiretap among Carol, Dave and Erin) pointed at Dave at once. On Night 2, Ivan's free Standard protection stopped the Katana on Heidi. That same night Niaj mapped Mallory's group, which held Heidi, so the Katana holder had to be one of its members. Judy then gave the game away on Day 3: she let slip the Yakuza-only word 'Ritualist' and dodged naming her Night 2 target, and she was hanged 8-4. Bob's Coroner exams confirmed each hang (Judy Ritualist, Dave Wiretap, Carol Puppeteer). Those exams turned the Yakuza's steady Innocent votes and public 'no claim, no action' stance into a case. The Yakuza made several more mistakes. They skipped the Night 1 kill. None of them built a fake claim. They voted as an obvious bloc. They never used their puppet, their 2 swaps or their 2 Ritualist guesses. They did kill the protector, Ivan, on Night 3, and Ivan died without having self-protected. Erin, holding the Katana, read Good to both Heidi's check and Mallory's chosen Seer pair. Mallory misread that pair as clearing Erin, and Heidi voted Innocent despite announcing Guilty, so Erin was acquitted on a 5-5 tie on Day 4. In the end, Mallory's random Night 4 pair (Heidi and Carol differ) exposed Carol. Erin was the last unclaimed player and was hanged on Day 6.

Outside log review (rules and bugs)
Review: medium, player confusionDay 4, Erin's trial: Frank publicly said 'voting Innocent on Erin' but his recorded secret vote was Guilty. Heidi publicly said 'voting Guilty on Erin' but her recorded vote was Innocent. The trial ended 5-5 and Erin was acquitted, so this decided the result. The two mismatches are mirror images, which could mean the harness swapped or misrecorded votes. It could also be players misusing the vote interface. Either way, the cast votes contradict the players' immediately preceding statements and should be checked.
Review: medium, player confusionMallory, the confirmed Seer, kept ignoring R19: the Katana holder appears Good to alignment checks that night. From her N3 chosen pair (Erin=Frank) and her N5 random pair (Grace=Erin), she concluded Erin was Good and Niaj was not Good. She voted Innocent on Erin on Day 4 and Day 6 and pushed suspicion onto Niaj, the real Cartographer. Erin held the Katana on both of those nights, so both results were fully explained. Niaj made a similar error on Day 5, claiming Mallory's N1 and N3 pairs 'can't both hold' alongside Frank's Oracle hits.
Review: low, moderator errorNight 3: the recorded visit list left out Heidi→Erin (the Sheriff check), as the automated Night check noted. The group sizes and Niaj's map still came out correct because Heidi was already linked through Ivan, but the visit record itself was incomplete.
Review: low, harness bugSeveral players gave empty answers cut off at max_tokens at high effort, and the harness retried at medium: Mallory three times (Day 4, Day 5, Day 6), Alice once and Niaj once on Day 4. After Niaj's fallback, no Niaj message appears, so a turn may have been lost during Erin's trial.
Review: low, player confusionOn Day 2 many players (Carol, Dave, Erin, Frank, Judy, Ivan) repeatedly asked Alice, the Scout, to post 'full group sizes, largest first'. The Scout only learns three names, never sizes; sizes come from the Cartographer. Carol also asked to check claims against 'Bob's reports', though Bob had no result.
Review: low, prompt problemBy round 7 of Day 2, Dave, Erin and Heidi each said that even a 10-word public message cost more than their remaining budget, so public speech was effectively locked. The budget seems tight enough that late-round discussion gets cut off, even though players spent the Day on routine messages.
Review: low, prompt problemIn the post-game debrief, Judy reported that the lessons and tips_feedback fields were not asked for in her prompt. This suggests the debrief prompt and the expected answer fields don't match.
